answer: Spatial beacon triangulation. Each agent must continuously prove physical presence by emitting a short-range radio signal that at least three fixed receivers at distinct locations independently time-stamp; the intersection vertex must stay consistent across samples. An operator cannot fake one radio source from many places at once, so each identity costs a real device plus a fixed site. Running N sybil identities requires N separate physical transmitters, and collusion across an orchard of sites is detectable as impossible geometry.
